title: finding(tests): three source-scanning tests hand-roll a comment stripper for CSS, YAML and JSONC — languages the shared masker deliberately does not answer for
body:
Found while converting the JavaScript carriers in objectui#9183 (PR objectui#9322). Not fixed
there: that card's subject is the naive-regex family pointed at **JavaScript**, and these three
are a different question with a different answer.

## What was measured

The objectui#9183 census re-derived the hand-rolled comment-stripper population to **32**
carriers. 29 were converted to `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`. The remaining **3** were left
alone on purpose, because their stripper is not pointed at JavaScript at all:

| carrier | what it actually strips |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/components/src/__tests__/empty-base-classes-override-friendly-8525.test.tsx` | CSS — `packages/components/src/index.css`, plus Tailwind's own `index.css` |
| `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` | Markdown (`content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`) and `.github/workflows/*.yml` |
| `packages/components/src/__tests__/skill-guide-data-table-binding.test.tsx` | JSONC, fed to `JSON.parse` |

`js-comment-mask.mjs` answers "is this span a comment, or code?" for **JavaScript** — its
scanner knows JS strings, templates and regex literals, and its corpus gate gauges it against a
JS parser. Aiming it at CSS or YAML would substitute a fresh guess for the shared answer, which
is the shape of the defect objectui#9183 exists to remove.

## Why this is worth a card rather than nothing

Each of the three carries the SAME hazard class in its own language, with no shared answer to
reach for:

- **CSS** has `/* */` and no `//`. A naive `//` rule is harmless there, but the block rule is
  not: a `/*` inside a `content:` string or a `url()` opens the same phantom span.
- **YAML** has `#` comments and no JS comment syntax at all, so a JS-shaped stripper aimed at a
  workflow file is answering a question the file never asks.
- **JSONC** is the interesting one. `skill-guide-data-table-binding` already reasons about the
  hazard in its own docblock (only `//` at line start or after whitespace is cut, "so a
  `https://` inside a string value is safe"), and a fourth file,
  `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/readme-flow-canvas-draft.test.ts:108`,
  independently hand-wrote a **string-aware** jsonc reader for exactly this reason, with a
  comment explaining why a blunt `replace` is wrong. So the tree already contains two separate
  private answers to "strip comments from JSONC", written by different hands.

## Deliberately NOT proposed here

- ⛔ Not "widen `js-comment-mask.mjs` to also do CSS/YAML/JSONC". Its value is that it answers
  one question for one language and is graded against a real parser for that language. A
  multi-language mode would dilute both.
- ⛔ Not "widen `check:comment-mask-corpus`". Its subject is the masker's own correctness, not
  who uses it (objectui#9183's triage ruling says so explicitly).

## What a fix might be

Decide, per language, whether a shared answer is warranted at all. The honest possibility is
that the answer is **no** for CSS and YAML (one carrier each, both narrow) and **yes** for
JSONC (two independent private readers already exist). Sizing that is the work; this card is
filed to record the measurement, not to presume the outcome.

Unmeasured, and stated as such: whether the CSS and YAML carriers can be made to give a wrong
answer today. objectui#9183 measured that for the 29 JavaScript carriers (none could); the same
diff was not run for these three, because there is no second implementation to diff them
against — which is the point of the card.

Refs objectui#9183 - PR objectui#9322
